Can a Casita Pay for Itself? The Real Value of Adding an ADU in Tucson

A backyard casita sounds like the ultimate flexible investment: space for family, a home office, or a potential rental.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

Compare the benefit with the costResearch permits, bids and comparable propertiesConsider your use and your exit strategyMore in Home Improvements ↗← All 24 articles

THE SHORT ANSWER

In Tucson and surrounding communities, casitas can offer meaningful lifestyle benefits even when the financial return is uncertain. Think through both your personal use and your exit strategy: would a future buyer value the same layout?

Compare the benefit with the cost

A backyard casita sounds like the ultimate flexible investment: space for family, a home office, or a potential rental. But does adding an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) actually increase your property's value enough to justify the cost? The answer depends on more than square footage. Buyers consider privacy, design, legal status, utility connections, and whether the extra space fits the neighborhood.

Research permits, bids and comparable properties

Before building, check local zoning and permit requirements, get detailed contractor bids, and research realistic rental income if leasing is part of the plan. Don't assume that a $150,000 construction bill adds $150,000 to the appraisal. Appraisers look for market evidence of how buyers value comparable properties with similar features, and an unpermitted or nonconforming unit can raise additional questions.

Consider your use and your exit strategy

In Tucson and surrounding communities, casitas can offer meaningful lifestyle benefits even when the financial return is uncertain. Think through both your personal use and your exit strategy: would a future buyer value the same layout? An independent residential appraisal can help you understand how similar improvements are reflected in the local market before making a major investment.
